key_insight: Temperature-dependent Raman and XRD reveal two distinct structural changes in SrLaCoNbO6: an isostructural octahedral distortion near 300°C and a symmetry-breaking phase transition near 750°C.
engineering_relevance: The study shows that low-cost laboratory spectroscopy and diffraction can diagnose hidden lattice instabilities in ordered perovskites, helping guide materials design for thermally robust functional oxides.
method: Combined temperature-dependent Raman spectroscopy and lab XRD from 25–900°C
Quantified octahedral distortion parameters for CoO6 and NbO6 units
Used group-theoretical analysis and Rietveld refinement to assign phases
evidence_signal: The abstract reports two clear anomalies supported by renormalized phonon frequency/linewidth changes and the appearance or suppression of characteristic XRD reflections.
watch_item: The identified transitions are based on a specific ordered double perovskite, so generalizing the same thresholds or distortion behavior to other compositions requires separate validation.
paper_title: Disentangling octahedral distortion and symmetry breaking in the ordered double perovskite SrLaCoNbO$_6$
